topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It frames the lecture by introducing the evolutionary view of cancer and outlining the key learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic drivers of clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations and epigenetic alterations confer selective growth advantages that drive Darwinian clonal succession in tissues.

topics.label: Stem cell hierarchy and cell of origin in tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the relationship between normal stem cell hierarchies, cancer stem cell models, and the cell of origin in cancer development.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and inflammatory promotion of tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how non-mutagenic microenvironmental factors, chronic inflammation, and supportive stroma promote cancer progression and provide therapeutic targets.

topics.label: Methods for investigating tumor evolution and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: It examines the experimental models, single-cell sequencing technologies, and spatial profiling tools used to study cancer evolution and cell interactions.

topics.label: Synthesis of multifactorial cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: It provides a comprehensive summary integrating genetic mutations, transcriptional states, cell of origin, and microenvironmental dynamics into a unified evolutionary framework of cancer.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the session and previews the upcoming lecture on cancer therapy.
